taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes recent genomic work and that P. slowinskii may be treated as a separate species or a subspecies of P. emoryi, and that P. emoryi itself may comprise two subspecies; Animal Diversity Web uses 'Great Plains rat snake' and the older Elaphe/Pantherophis placement.
fieldMarks: Gray to light-brown ground colour with large brown blotches down the midline of the back, flanked by two rows of smaller blotches.
A V- or spear-point mark on the head leading toward the neck.
Belly is a black-and-white checkerboard with stripes under the tail; scales slightly keeled; anal plate divided.
behavior: Mainly nocturnal forager; hides by day under rocks, logs, boards, in crevices and small mammal burrows.
Semi-arboreal; climbs high in trees to hunt birds; also swims.
Eats mainly rodents plus birds and eggs, and occasionally snakes, lizards and frogs; kills by constriction.
When agitated shakes the tail (audible in dry leaf litter, often mistaken for a rattlesnake), strikes and releases musk; hibernates alone.
habitat: Fields, hill prairie, brushy areas, woodlands, riparian areas, canyons, barnyards and abandoned buildings; avoids heavily forested regions.
Also rocky hillsides and areas near springs and cave entrances.
range: Southwestern Illinois, Missouri, southern South Dakota and southeastern Colorado south to San Luis Potosi and Veracruz, through most of Texas, with a disjunct population in eastern Utah and western Colorado. Not found in Canada.
